title: Numbers Divisible by Each Own Digit
statement:
Call a positive integer self-checking when it is divisible by every one of its own digits. A number that contains the digit 0 is never self-checking, because you cannot divide by zero.

Given left and right, return all self-checking numbers in the range [left, right] (both ends included), in increasing order.

examples.why: 24 works: 24 % 2 = 0 and 24 % 4 = 0. 14 fails because 14 % 4 = 2, and 20 contains a 0.
Every number in this range has a 0 digit.

hints: Handle one number at a time. How do you visit each of its digits without converting it to a string?
Repeatedly take x % 10 for the last digit and divide x by 10 (rounding down) to drop it.
Reject the number as soon as a digit is 0 or does not divide the original number.

explain.intuition: The range is small, so checking every number directly is the intended solution. The only skill is walking the digits of a number: x % 10 is the last digit and Math.floor(x / 10) removes it. Keep a copy of the original number, because the divisibility test is always against the whole number, not the shrinking remainder.
steps: For each v from left to right, set x = v.
While x > 0: let d = x % 10. If d === 0 or v % d !== 0, reject v.
Otherwise drop the digit with x = Math.floor(x / 10).
If the loop finishes without rejecting, add v to the result.
pitfalls: Dividing by a zero digit. In JavaScript v % 0 is NaN, which is not equal to 0, so it happens to reject; in Python it raises an error. Check for 0 explicitly.
Testing divisibility against the shrinking x instead of the original number v.
Using x / 10 without flooring in JavaScript, which never reaches 0 cleanly.

solutions.title: Check digits as characters
solutions.idea: Turn each number into a string and test every character.

solutions.title: Peel digits with % and /
solutions.idea: Walk the digits arithmetically and stop at the first zero or non-divisor.

followups: The range goes up to 10¹⁸. You can no longer check every number. How would a digit DP count them?
Return only how many self-checking numbers there are in many different ranges. What would you precompute?
